svg.desc: BLE Vehicle-Key Three Attack Paths: Replay / Relay / Protocol Flaw Exploitation, academic black-and-white line diagram
svg.text: BLE Vehicle-Key Attack Paths
Replay · Relay · Protocol Flaw Exploitation (shared recon → three parallel paths → verdict)
Recon: protocol intelligence
Feeds all three paths
App reverse engineering
frame format / UUID / handle map
crypto flow (CBC / ECDH / GCM)
→ flaw profile: downgrade feasibility / nonce gen / key derivation
feeds Path 3
BLE frame capture
Ellisys air-interface / Bumble HCI snoop
broadcast payload (vendor ID / session seed / fingerprint)
session frame sequence (plaintext without pairing)
feeds Paths 1 & 2; reveals flaws with App analysis
Recon outputs
ad format / session seed → key derivation
GATT handle / command semantics
busy/idle window profile (duty cycle / reject codes)
Flaw checklist: no freshness? nonce reuse? downgrade?
Path 1
Path 2
Path 3
Path 1: Replay
Simplest when no session binding
Precondition
no nonce / counter / timestamp in frames
or pairing not enabled (no LE Secure Connections)
determined during recon
Action
Bumble parses captured frames → GATT write semantics
e.g. handle=X, value=unlock()
dongle connects as Central, resends original frames
replay(handle, value) → vehicle
no session forgery — reuses original frame semantics
Vehicle executes → missing freshness protection
Rejected → check crypto flaws in Path 3
Path 2: Relay
Immune to application-layer encryption
Precondition
target App is scan-driven (finds car via broadcast)
reconnect-driven App needs MAC clone + connect race
determined during recon
Action (two-dongle bidirectional relay)
nRF#2 as Peripheral: clones vehicle ad, lures phone
nRF#1 as Central: connects to real vehicle
relays application-layer PDUs — re-encrypts per hop:
phone ↔ #2 one LTK / #1 ↔ car another LTK
challenge-response passes through verbatim
app-layer crypto cannot stop it — the essence of relay
Ellisys captures both hops live, validates relay
Link holds with full function → no proximity binding
(no UWB ranging / no enforced RSSI threshold)
Path 3: Protocol Flaw Exploitation
Hypothetical example: KNOB-class downgrade + nonce misuse
Precondition (hypothetical flaws)
protocol design permits MitM-forced negotiation downgrade
(e.g. CVE-2019-9506 class: unbound key-length negotiation)
implementation flaw in nonce generation / key derivation
Action (cryptographic attack)
scan ads + trigger handshake → collect ciphertext pairs
window-racing connect, repeatedly induce renegotiation
MitM-forced downgrade → brute-force small key space
nonce reuse → known-plaintext XOR → keystream recovery
GHASH H factorization → forged authentication tag
recover session key → forge valid frames (probe → unlock → relock)
both protocol-design and implementation flaws — combined to be lethal
Unlock succeeds → unbound negotiation + nonce uniqueness broken
strong link crypto cannot help — negotiation & implementation flaws break AEAD
Verdict & Output
any path succeeds → vulnerability confirmed, written to Playbook
Path 1 → flaw: no freshness protection (no nonce / counter / timestamp)
Path 2 → flaw: no proximity binding (no UWB ranging / RSSI threshold)
Path 3 → flaw: unbound negotiation (KNOB-class) + nonce reuse / key derivation defect
Three complementary paths — crypto strength only affects Path 1, not Paths 2 or 3
Hardware reuse: Ellisys observes throughout; nRF52840 #1 switches Observer / Central, #2 acts as Peripheral when needed
Toolchain: Bumble scripted driving · custom AOSP ROM provides HookLogic-X observation primitives on the App side
Legend
solid arrow: control / data flow
dotted: observation (non-intrusive)
